slides.texte_overlay:
Things that make you quietly
confident in any room
Take up your space. Sit back in the chair, both feet on the floor, arms off your chest. You don't need to spread out like a king. You just stop trying to look smaller than you are.
Introduce yourself first. Walk up, hand out, "Hi, I'm Sam." Most people wait to be introduced and just stand there. Going first takes two seconds of nerve and sets the tone for the whole night.
Take a compliment with a simple thank you. No "Oh, this old thing?" No pushing it away. Just "Thanks, I appreciate that." Taking it calmly says you know your worth without needing to prove it.
Walk in with something on your mind. Five minutes a day of history, art or science gives you real things to think and talk about. Confidence comes a lot easier when your head isn't empty.
slides.texte_sophia: Walk in with something on your mind. A micro-learning app like the Sophia app gives you five minutes a day of history, art or science. Confidence comes easier when your head isn't empty.

slides.texte_overlay: Stop checking yourself in every reflection. Windows, phone screen, the mirror behind the bar. Check once before you leave, then forget it. Confident people aren't watching themselves, they're watching the room.
Disagree calmly. "I see it differently, actually." Then explain without raising your voice. You don't need to win, and you don't need to fold. Holding a view politely is rare, and people respect it.
Be fine with leaving early. "I'm heading out, great night." No long excuses, no guilt. Doing what you want without needing everyone's approval is the quietest kind of confidence there is.
